Both files written.

**Gold file / order of reading.** I used `gold.json` (no `golden.json` in the case dir), and I read `ranked.json` in full before opening it.

**Shape.** The answer is a flat array of 40 paths — single-repo form, the same form `gold.json` uses. No flattening was needed.

**Metrics** (from `score_arm.py`, verbatim; hits 4 / gold_total 8):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| recall@10 | 0.25 |
| recall@20 | 0.25 |
| recall@25 | 0.25 |
| recall@50 | 0.50 (degenerate — list is 40 long) |
| recall@75 | 0.50 (degenerate) |

| MRR | 1.00 |

`score_arm.py` does not emit precision@10, precision@20, F1@20 or F1_full_list — the only precision it computes is `precision@5` (score_arm.py:210). I did not hand-compute the missing ones.

**found** (rank): `packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/service/EmailWorkflowService.ts` (1), `packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts` (2), `packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/types.ts` (33), `packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendWorkflowEmails.ts` (34).

**missed_gold**: `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-04-15/controllers/bookings.controller.ts`, `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/input.service.ts`, `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts`.

**Surface verdict: NOT comparable.** One reason: prompt caching was active — `cache_read=1,535,089`, `cache_creation=162,529`, so the $2.78 is a warm-cache figure and not comparable to cold runs. The tool surface itself is clean: 23 calls, all plumbline MCP plus 2 ToolSearch (schema loading, exempt); no filesystem or shell tool; `stakeout`, the retriever's own search tool, fired 6 times. My tally from `commands.log` matches the scorer's exactly. Note the scorer's own surface block reports `not_comparable: []` — it does not apply the cache rule; I preserved it under `surface.scorer_reported` and set the top-level verdict from the cache evidence.

**What the misses share.** All four sit outside the `packages/features/**` workflow-and-booking layer the run worked in, and each belongs to a boundary register rather than a service register: two are v2 API edge files (`bookings.controller.ts`, `input.service.ts`), one is the HTTP cron entrypoint for the same workflow email path whose service layer the run did rank first (`scheduleEmailReminders.ts`), and one is the shared schema module (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts`). The run's four hits are all the service/type/task interior of the email-workflow path; what it did not reach is that path's inbound edge — request controllers, input coercion, the API route handler — and the schema definition those edges validate against. Everything retrieved past rank 2 stayed inside the same feature interior, extending laterally (reminder scheduling, branding, booking handlers, page props) rather than upward to the callers or downward to the shared schema.
